workflow.step1: Start calibration mode and wait for fast readings.
workflow.step3: Place a known weight and enter its kg value.
workflow.step4: Capture the weighted reading and save.

tempco.title: Temperature compensation
tempco.description: Load cells drift with temperature. The backend smooths the temperature with an exponential moving average (EMA) to damp short transients (e.g. sunrise), then corrects the reported weight as raw − coeff · (EMA(temp) − ref) on read; the raw weight is never changed.
tempco.sourceHint: Ambient tracks the cell body closely in steady state and is the recommended default.

errors.refTemp: Reference temperature must be a number (°C).

perHive.manualSaveHint: Switch hives to edit another scale; all edits are sent together when you save. Hives 3 and up are only written when changed.

tempco.refHint: The temperature at which the scales read true, i.e. the one they were tared and spanned at. The correction is zero there; fitting leaves it alone unless you ask it to.
tempco.setRefTempHint: Replaces the reference with the mean temperature of the fitted window. Leave off if the scale was calibrated at a known temperature.
tempco.fitSummary: {{scaleName}}: {{coeff}} kg/°C, R² {{r2}} over {{n}} readings from {{min}}–{{max}} °C (window mean {{mean}} °C).
tempco.lowRSquared: R² below 0.5: temperature explains little of this drift. Fit over a stretch with a constant load and a wide day/night swing.
tempco.autoFitHint: Auto-fit regresses the selected hive's stored weight over the lookback window against the EMA-smoothed selected temperature. "Fit only" fills the coefficient for review before you save; "Fit & apply" stores it and enables compensation. For a clean fit, pick a window where the physical load is constant and the temperature swings.

errors.lookback: Lookback must be a whole number of days between 1 and 90.

toasts.fitFilled: {{scaleName}}: {{coeff}} kg/°C (R²={{r2}}, n={{n}}). Filled in — review and save.

board.cardDescription: Firmware of this HiveHub and of the HiveInside nodes and HiveTraffic counters it carries. Uploading registers a release; approving (hub) or relaying (nodes) installs it.
board.approveConfirm:
Approve firmware {{version}} and flash it over the air?

The HiveHub installs it on its next check-in and reboots. A remote device that fails mid-update may need physical access to recover.
board.otherBoards: Also uploaded for another board (not applied to this {{board}} device): {{releases}}. A build only reaches a device whose board matches — check the board when uploading.
board.otherBoardsUnknown: Also uploaded for another board (not applied to this device): {{releases}}. A build only reaches a device whose board matches — check the board when uploading.

relays.alreadyQueued: A relay is already queued for this node
relays.confirm:
Relay {{name}} {{version}} to {{hive}}?

The HiveHub picks this up on its next upload cycle — normally within about 10 minutes, or whatever send interval this device uses. It then streams the image over BLE for a few minutes and the node reboots into it. The node must be awake and in range, or the relay fails and has to be queued again.

tooltip.title: Tests performed
tooltip.description: Each detector runs on every measurement pass against the last 14 days of weight and hive-temperature data.

detectors.title: Pre-swarm watch (Phase 1)
detectors.detail: 24h brood-nest temperature std-dev ≥ 1.5× the 7-day baseline → watch.

detectors.title: Imminent swarm (Phase 2)
detectors.detail: Brood temp ≥ 1.5 °C above 4h baseline, still rising ≥ 0.5 °C/h, above 36.5 °C → warning.

detectors.title: Swarm event (Phase 3)
detectors.detail: Weight drop ≥ 1.5 kg within ≤ 30 min. Daytime (09–17) → critical, otherwise warning.

detectors.title: Queenlessness (fallback, no audio)
detectors.detail: Active season + 7d hive-temp std-dev > 1.0 °C AND |weight change| < 0.2 kg → warning.

detectors.title: Robbing
detectors.detail: Sustained weight loss ≥ 0.4 kg/h for ≥ 30 min, no swarm signature. Late afternoon (15–19) → warning, else watch.

detectors.title: Foraging intensity
detectors.detail: 24h weight delta: ≥ 1.0 kg = strong flow (info), ≥ 0.2 kg = moderate (info), ≤ −0.2 kg = negative (watch).

detectors.title: Brood cycle / colony state
detectors.detail: 24h hive-temp std-dev < 0.5 °C around 34–35 °C = active brood (info); > 2.0 °C = broodless / weak (watch).

detectors.title: Absconding / collapse trend
detectors.detail: 14d weight loss > 100 g/day AND widening daily temp std-dev (positive slope) → watch.

detectors.title: Winter survival risk (Oct–Feb)
detectors.detail: Min hive temp 7d < ambient mean + 2 °C, or weight loss > 300 g/week. Both → warning, one → watch.

detectors.title: Harvest window
detectors.detail: Earlier 7d gain > 2 kg/week, now < 0.3 kg/week for ≥ 4 days → info.

traffic.title: HiveTraffic bee counters
traffic.description: Night mode and emitter banks for every HiveTraffic counter paired to this hub. The IR emitters are by far the largest item in a counter's power budget, so these settings decide whether it fits an off-grid supply.
traffic.readOnly: Only device owners and admins can change these settings. Your role is “{{role}}”.
traffic.saved: Bee counter settings saved. Counters pick them up on the next check-in.
traffic.appliesToAll: Applies to every HiveTraffic counter paired to this device. The counter is told on the hub's next upload cycle.

status.title: Counters right now
status.none: No HiveTraffic counter reported in the latest reading.
status.banksUnknown: Emitter banks not reported (counter firmware older than 0.3.0)

night.title: Night mode
night.description: Honey bees are diurnal — flight needs light and stops below about 10 °C anyway. During this window the counter stops sensing to save power. It keeps advertising, so readings and firmware updates still work.
night.windowHelp: The window may cross midnight (e.g. 20:00 → 06:00). Setting start and end to the same time makes the window empty — it never applies — rather than covering the whole day. Leave a margin around dusk and dawn: activity peaks just before sunset and sunrise.
night.emptyWindow: Start and end are the same, so the window is empty and night mode would never apply.
night.wrapsMidnight: The window crosses midnight: from {{start}} until {{end}} the next morning.
night.timezoneHelp: The hub's clock runs in UTC. Without the right timezone the window is off by your UTC offset and drifts by an hour at each daylight-saving change.
night.maxTrafficHelp: Postpone night mode while more than this many crossings (in + out) were counted in the last upload cycle, so a colony still flying late on a summer evening is not cut off. 0 goes by the clock only.

banks.title: Emitter banks
banks.description: The counter's IR emitters are switched in three banks of eight gates. Each bank draws about 80 mA. Switch one off if the entrance is narrower than 24 gates, part of it is closed, or the supply cannot carry the whole board.
banks.current_one: {{count}} bank on · about {{ma}} mA on the counter's 3.3 V rail
banks.current_other: {{count}} banks on · about {{ma}} mA on the counter's 3.3 V rail
banks.help: A switched-off bank does not count its gates at all, so totals drop roughly in proportion — do not compare a narrowed counter with its own history. At least one bank must stay on; unpair a counter that should count nothing.
banks.firmwareNote: Needs counter firmware 0.3.0 or newer. The setting is re-sent after every counter reset.

errors.noBank: At least one emitter bank must stay on — unpair the counter instead.

hubAccess.title: Hub access
hubAccess.description: Reach the hub on site without opening the enclosure, and set how long an inspection may run.
hubAccess.readOnly: Only device owners and admins can change these settings. Your role is “{{role}}”.

ap.title: Setup access point
ap.description: Opens the hub's HiveHub-Setup Wi-Fi network, the same as a short press on the setup button: change Wi-Fi, pair sensors or download the SD card data.
ap.confirmTiming_one: The request is queued. The hub is asleep between cycles, so the access point opens after its next check-in — up to {{count}} minute from now.
ap.confirmTiming_other: The request is queued. The hub is asleep between cycles, so the access point opens after its next check-in — up to {{count}} minutes from now.
ap.confirmTimingUnknown: The request is queued. The hub is asleep between cycles, so the access point opens after its next check-in — up to one send interval from now.
ap.confirmOffline: While the access point is open the hub is off Wi-Fi and sends no readings.
ap.confirmTimeout: It closes by itself after the setup portal timeout if nobody connects, so only start it when someone is at the hive.
ap.queued: Access point queued. It opens after the hub's next check-in.
ap.failed: Could not queue the access point

inspection.description: A safety net: an inspection ends by itself after this many minutes, so a forgotten button press does not blank a hive's data indefinitely. Default 60.
inspection.label: Timeout (minutes, 1–1440)

health.title: Sensor health
health.descriptionAt: Sensor health from the last check-in · {{ago}}.
health.noData: No sensor health reported yet — it appears once the device sends its first reading.
health.noHiveSensors: No sensors reported for this hive.
health.faultNote: The hub reports its own subsystems as pass/fail — it sends no error code for them, so each fault above says what failed instead. The entrance counter does report a status code, and it is shown with the fault wherever one was read.

hubReason.sht_ok: The ambient sensor did not return a valid reading this cycle, so this check-in carries no ambient temperature or humidity. Usually an I²C bus or wiring fault; a sensor that was never detected at boot reads the same way.
hubReason.rtc_ok: The real-time clock did not answer on the I²C bus. Timestamps fall back to network time, so a reading taken while offline can be misdated.
hubReason.sd_ok: The SD card was not mounted this cycle — missing, unreadable, or an SPI/wiring fault. Readings are not buffered to the card while this persists.
hubReason.mic_ok: The microphone capture returned no usable samples, so this check-in carries no acoustic bands.
hubReason.mic_left_ok: The left microphone returned no usable samples.
hubReason.mic_right_ok: The right microphone returned no usable samples.
hubReason.battery_monitor_ok: The battery fuel gauge did not answer on the I²C bus — battery voltage and state of charge are missing from this check-in.
hubReason.solar_monitor_ok: The solar monitor did not answer on the I²C bus — solar voltage, current and power are missing from this check-in.

reason.scale: A scale is configured for this hive but produced no usable reading this cycle, so this check-in carries no weight for it.
reason.inHive: No advertisement from the paired {{kind}} during this cycle's BLE scan — out of range, flat battery, or powered off.
reason.notHeardInRange: Not heard in the loaded range.
reason.counter: The entrance counter did not answer its GATT read this cycle — out of range, powered off, or busy when HiveHub dialled.
reason.notAnsweredInRange: It has not answered in the loaded range.
reason.hiveheart: The HiveHeart was not heard this cycle — out of range, flat battery, or powered off.

hubStatus.description: Uplink, clock and power of the HiveHub itself.
hubStatus.noData: No reading received from this hub yet.
hubStatus.staleWarning: No reading for {{ago}} — the hub has missed several check-ins.

hiveCards.empty: No hives reported by this device yet.
hiveCards.trafficTitle: Bees in/out during the last interval

audio.title: Hive audio
audio.description: Ask a hive's HiveInside node to record, then listen to it here. The hub collects the request on its next wake, so a recording appears within one reporting interval rather than immediately.
audio.noNodes: No HiveInside node is paired on this hub. Only HiveInside has a microphone — a HolyIot or RuuviTag beacon cannot record.
audio.nextWake: Reaches the hub on its next wake.
audio.viewerNote: An owner or admin can request a recording.
audio.lengthHint: Shorter is usually better: 10–20 seconds is enough to hear what an insight flagged, and costs less battery and less time with the hive off the air — a connected node neither advertises nor samples.
audio.requestSuccess: Recording requested. It reaches the hub on its next wake.
audio.requestError: The request could not be queued: {{message}}
audio.empty: No recordings yet. Ask a hive to record and it will appear here. A session is 10–60 seconds of 16 kHz audio pulled off the node over BLE.
audio.waitingNote: Waiting for the hub to wake and pick this up — nothing recorded yet. A request the hub has not collected within 45 minutes is marked failed.
audio.streamingNote: Recording — the audio appears here as it arrives.
audio.streamingPartial: Still recording — this is what has arrived so far. Play it again when the session ends to hear the whole thing.
audio.deleteConfirm: Delete this recording? Nothing else ever will — there is no automatic clean-up.

cause.dropped: the node could not push audio out fast enough
cause.gaps: packets were lost on the air
cause.hubBuffer: the hub's upload fell behind its buffer

quality.gapNote: Audio either side of a gap is real, but the join is not. Cause: {{causes}}.
quality.clippingNote: Lower the gain for a cleaner recording.
quality.unknownNote: The hub never reported on this session, so nothing checked whether the audio is whole. What is here plays.
